questions.q: Why is S3 a good first resource to deploy by hand from the CLI, per this lesson?
options: It has no server to provision and no network to configure, while still exercising real IAM identity and policy concepts
S3 is the only AWS service that can be controlled through the CLI
S3 is free and never incurs any cost under any circumstances
S3 requires no IAM permissions of any kind to use
questions.explain: S3's simplicity (no compute/network provisioning) makes it a clean first hands-on target while still touching real IAM concepts.

questions.q: What does it mean that S3 bucket names are "globally unique"?
options: A bucket name must be unique across every AWS account on Earth, not just within your own account or region
Bucket names only need to be unique within your own AWS account
Bucket names only need to be unique within a single AWS region
AWS assigns bucket names automatically, so uniqueness is never a concern
questions.explain: This global uniqueness constraint is why aws s3 mb can fail with BucketAlreadyExists even if you've never used that name yourself.

questions.q: Per this lesson's "verify, don't assume" principle, what actually confirms a deploy worked?
options: Explicitly checking the resource, e.g. with aws s3 ls or downloading the object back, rather than just trusting a command's clean exit
Nothing — a command returning without an error message is always sufficient proof
Waiting 24 hours before assuming anything succeeded
Checking the AWS billing dashboard only
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly distinguishes a clean exit code from actual verification, like running aws s3 ls to confirm the object exists.

questions.q: Why does aws s3 rb fail on a bucket that still contains an object, and what does that prevent?
options: It's a deliberate safety guard against accidentally deleting a bucket full of data — the object must be removed first with aws s3 rm
It's a bug in the AWS CLI with no intentional purpose
rb can never delete any bucket under any circumstances, empty or not
AWS requires a support ticket before any bucket can be deleted
questions.explain: Requiring an empty bucket before removal is a deliberate guard rail against accidental data loss.

questions.q: What is the full round-trip sequence of commands this lesson walks through?
options: aws s3 mb (create) → aws s3 cp (upload) → aws s3 ls / cp - (verify) → aws s3 rm then rb (clean up)
aws configure → aws s3 ls → aws iam list-users, with no cleanup step
aws s3 rb → aws s3 mb → aws s3 cp, in that order
A single command that handles create, verify, and cleanup automatically
questions.explain: This is the exact sequence demonstrated: create, upload, verify, then clean up by removing the object and finally the bucket.
